summary: American Samoa is NOT a closed ban on pet rats - its status is genuinely unsettled. The territory's import rules (Regulation 24, Ch. 3, 1978) prohibit importing enumerated 'miscellaneous pets' - hamsters and rabbits are named - but NEITHER Rattus rattus NOR R. norvegicus appears on that list. A $2 import permit + a government-endorsed health certificate are required for domestic-animal import (sec. 24.0306), and the Director of Agriculture has discretion (sec. 24.0318(b)) to decide whether an unlisted animal counts as a prohibited 'miscellaneous pet' - so pet rats are unresolved at the agency level, not automatically banned. In-territory KEEPING isn't separately regulated (no 'banned to keep' list; the anti-rodent duties in ASCA sec. 20.1716 target wharf/vessel operators, not pet owners). The hard constraint is IMPORT: it needs the permit + health cert + a favorable Director determination, and because American Samoa is outside the US customs territory, shipments even from the US mainland are treated as international imports.

keep.why: Law regulates IMPORT, not in-territory possession; no provision of ASCA Title 25 or Regulation 24 prohibits keeping a rat already present, and no 'banned-to-keep' species list exists. ASCA sec. 20.1716 anti-rodent duties apply to wharf/vessel operators, not pet keepers.
keep.governing_law: Am. Samoa Reg. 24.0306 / 24.0318 (1978); ASCA sec. 20.1716; 19 CFR sec. 7.2 (outside US customs territory); 50 CFR Part 14 (USFWS).

breed.why: No breeding-specific prohibition or small-mammal breeding-licence scheme found; unaddressed by current regulation. The 1978 rules + the Director's sec. 24.0318(b) discretionary catch-all leave real uncertainty.
breed.governing_law: Am. Samoa Reg. 24.0306 / 24.0318 (1978); ASCA sec. 20.1716; 19 CFR sec. 7.2 (outside US customs territory); 50 CFR Part 14 (USFWS).

sell_give.why: No sale/transfer prohibition for pet rodents found in ASCA Title 25 or Regulation 24; no CITES domestic-sales legislation identified. In-territory transfer is unaddressed.
sell_give.governing_law: Am. Samoa Reg. 24.0306 / 24.0318 (1978); ASCA sec. 20.1716; 19 CFR sec. 7.2 (outside US customs territory); 50 CFR Part 14 (USFWS).

transport.why: Importing any rodent needs (a) a $2 import permit obtained in advance from the Dept of Agriculture (sec. 24.0306), (b) a government-endorsed veterinary health certificate, and (c) clearance by the Chief Quarantine Officer at Pago Pago - PLUS a favorable sec. 24.0318(b) Director determination that pet rats aren't 'miscellaneous pets' (no on-island quarantine facility, so failure = return to origin). American Samoa is outside US customs territory; USFWS Form 3-177 applies if routed through a US designated port. Never release.
transport.governing_law: Am. Samoa Reg. 24.0306 / 24.0318 (1978); ASCA sec. 20.1716; 19 CFR sec. 7.2 (outside US customs territory); 50 CFR Part 14 (USFWS).

restrictions.summary: American Samoa doesn't list rats as prohibited and doesn't regulate in-territory keeping - but IMPORT needs a $2 permit + health certificate + a favorable Director determination (sec. 24.0318(b)) that pet rats aren't 'miscellaneous pets.' Get that written determination BEFORE shipping one (no on-island quarantine = denied animals are returned). Never release.
steps: Request a written sec. 24.0318(b) Director determination that pet rats aren't a prohibited 'miscellaneous pet'
If favorable: apply for the sec. 24.0306 import permit ($2) + a USDA-endorsed health certificate
restrictions.where_to_file: American Samoa Dept of Agriculture - Plant & Animal Quarantine Division

inquiry_focus: (1) Under Regulation 24.0318(b), has the Director of Agriculture issued a written determination classifying domesticated pet rats (Rattus norvegicus or Rattus rattus) as a prohibited 'miscellaneous pet'? If no determination exists, what is the process to request one? (2) If pet rats aren't categorically prohibited, what documentation (import-permit form, health-certificate specs, approved-origin list) is required under sec. 24.0306, and the processing time? (3) Is there a published list of species currently approved or denied under sec. 24.0318(b)?
